business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Structural Drafting

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: New Zealand (Unitary National Jurisdiction; non-resident International Company special-purpose vehicle)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation with statutory recognition of Treaty of Waitangi principles and Māori customary considerations; unitary national company-registry regime without sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: New Zealand-China Free Trade Agreement (2008) as upgraded by the Investment and Services Protocol (in force 2022)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP; in force 30 December 2018)
New Zealand-Singapore Closer Economic Partnership and Investment Protocol (2001; amended 2019)
New Zealand-Australia Closer Economic Relations Trade Agreement (CER; 1983, as amended)
New Zealand-United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (in force 31 May 2023)
New Zealand-European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 May 2024)
New Zealand-China Double Taxation Agreement (1986, as amended by the 2019 Protocol)
New Zealand-Hong Kong SAR Double Taxation Agreement (2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Act 2017 and the 2019 Trusts Act amendments) ss 5, 10-17, 22-22E, 31, 32, 40, 49-53; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2011; Companies Act 1993 ss 18-22, 87-91, 188-196 and ss 201-213 (share registers, registered office, and director residency/agent requirements); Companies (Register of Charges) Act 1993; Trusts Act 2019; Income Tax Act 2007 (non-resident company residency, controlled foreign company, and DTA tie-breaker rules); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; United Nations Act 1946; Russia Sanctions Act 2022; and the New Zealand Companies Office fee schedules made under the Companies Act 1993.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (no central public UBO register currently in force; registered shareholders and their holdings appear on the publicly searchable New Zealand Companies Register; natural-person beneficial-ownership data is collected and verified internally by the reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and is disclosed only to the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit, AML/CFT supervisors, the NZ Police, Inland Revenue, and the courts on lawful demand; nominee shareholders are permitted but the underlying UBO must be identified to the reporting entity and the company's records must reflect the true beneficial interest).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the full valid passport (biometric data page) of each proposed director, each registered shareholder, and every ultimate beneficial owner of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil-law notary public or authorized commissioner for oaths in the document owner's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the origin state (e.g., PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ACRA Singapore, Hong Kong High Court, New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade); if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention party, chain consular legalization via the New Zealand embassy or consulate in the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing for every corporate shareholder and each intermediate holding entity in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or licensed registered agent of the intermediate jurisdiction (e.g., Companies Registry of Hong Kong, ACRA Singapore, New Zealand Companies Office, PRC SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the registry's seal or of the registered agent's certifying signature; consular legalization required only if the issuing jurisdiction is not a Hague Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming identity, account conduct, source of funds, and financial standing of the funding shareholder or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The licensed commercial bank maintaining the account of the funding party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer together with SWIFT/authenticated bank confirmation; apostille not required under prevailing NZ AML/CFT market practice for bank letters, but notarization is mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extracts of the shareholders' register and directors' register for each corporate UBO or intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or registered agent of the corporate UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member; otherwise consular legalization through the New Zealand diplomatic post in the origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Business registration certificate and tax identification certificate of the ultimate operating or trade principal entity (e.g., PRC business licence issued by SAMR) where such entity is the economic beneficiary of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the PRC or equivalent competent registry in the operating jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarial certification followed by PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille; New Zealand Embassy consular legalization is not required because the PRC and New Zealand are reciprocal members of the Hague Apostille Convention

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, ss. 12-25 (incorporation, name and constitution), ss. 42-47 (share issue and capital), ss. 118-127 (directors and board), ss. 128-132 (meetings and resolutions), ss. 189-201 (company records); Companies (Fees) Regulations 2008; Financial Reporting Act 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ngāari Rangahau Tūmatanui), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online filing via companiesoffice.govt.nz and the NZBN register (RealMe authenticated portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (filed electronically under s. 12 of the Companies Act 1993 through the Companies Office 'Incorporate a Company' online service); issuance is evidenced by the Certificate of Incorporation and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement under New Zealand law. A company may incorporate with one share of no par value issued for NZ$1.00 (or unpaid/partly paid if permitted by the constitution). For an International Company operating in a tax-exempt offshore capacity, initial capital is usually the subscription monies for 100 ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each, held in the corporate bank account; no statutory capital deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
[COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company') - RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS passed in writing pursuant to s. 122 of the Companies Act 1993 (no meeting necessary).
1. ADOPTION OF CONSTITUTION: RESOLVED that the constitution of the Company annexed to the Application for Registration be adopted as the constitution of the Company with full force and effect.
2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: RESOLVED that the allotment and issue of 100 ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each to [SUBSCRIBER], being fully paid in cash, be approved; the directors are authorized to enter the allotment in the share register and to issue share certificates.
3. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [STREET ADDRESS, CITY, NEW ZEALAND], which shall be recorded with the Registrar of Companies as the registered office and address for service.
4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [NAME] be appointed as a director and Chairperson, that [NAME] be appointed as Chief Executive Officer, and that [NAME] (if required) be appointed as Company Secretary, each to hold office under the Companies Act 1993 with authority to sign statutory filings and declarations.
5. BANKING AND OPERATIONAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that any one director or the Company Secretary be authorized to open and operate corporate bank accounts, to execute client contracts for Building Information Modeling (BIM), structural CAD drafting and civil-infrastructure engineering design outsourcing (ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330), and to appoint professional advisers.
6. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the directors be authorized to do all acts and execute all documents necessary to give effect to these resolutions and to carry on the Company's business lawfully in New Zealand and abroad.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Clearance and Availability Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register name search (companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Review the proposed company name against the public Companies Register to ensure it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and does not breach ss. 22-24 of the Companies Act 1993 (restricted words require Registrar approval). Confirm that the name accurately reflects the target sector (civil infrastructure BIM/CAD) and is acceptable for an International Company. Save the name-search report as evidence.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two alternative names
Name search report from the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the name, the applicant may amend the name and re-file; if an objection is lodged by a third party, the Registrar will notify the applicant, who may respond in writing within 20 working days. A name decision may be appealed to the New Zealand High Court under s. 25 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Governing Documents, Director Consents and Office Address
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating agent / applicant's New Zealand counsel (submission prepared on the Companies Office portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution (statutory default rules or bespoke articles, including permitted non-resident ownership and offshore service restrictions for the International Company), complete the shareholder/subscriber list, obtain signed consents to act as a director in accordance with s. 151 of the Companies Act 1993, and fix a physical registered office address in New Zealand (not a P.O. Box). A street address for service outside the registered office may also be filed.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act as director
Registered office physical address in New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the documents for defect, correct and resubmit the affected pages through the online workspace; the incorporation agent may electronically amend attachments before lodgment. Continued refusal may be contested by way of written representations to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Application and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Online incorporation service via RealMe/NZBN authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Companies Office portal with a verified RealMe identity, select 'Incorporate a company', enter the company name, constitution, director details, shareholder details, registered office, and financial year-end (31 March), and submit the Application for Registration of a Company. Pay the statutory incorporation fee of NZ$150 (approximately USD 93) by credit card or online banking.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant has 30 days to make corrections through the online workspace; if abandoned, the fee is refundable upon written request under the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2008.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies / New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar registers the company, issues the Certificate of Incorporation in electronic form, and allocates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) automatically. Verify the registered details (entity number, name, date of incorporation, directors, registered office) on the public Companies Register and download the certificate for banking and licensing use.
required_dossiers: Companies Register extract for good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or register entry contains a clerical error (name, date, director details), file a Notice of Change with supporting evidence to have the Companies Office correct the record promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Corporate Bank Account and Post-Incorporation Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / Company Secretary and commercial bank (ASB, ANZ, BNP Paribas NZ or similar) regulated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass written resolutions adopting the draft First Board Resolution (including ratification of share subscription, registered office, officer appointments and banking mandate). Open the corporate bank account in the company's name (non-resident directors permitted), obtain SWIFT/BIC and account details for wire-transfer and Wise payment rails, and authorize two directors as signatories. File any post-registration changes (e.g., actual registered office or service address) with the Companies Office.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written resolution signed by all directors
Director identification (passport) and proof of address
Bank account application and beneficial-ownership declarations (AML/CFT Act 2009)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank seeks additional beneficial ownership information for an offshore International Company, provide an authenticated Companies Register extract, a letter of good standing, and a written confirmation of the company's tax-exempt status; if the bank declines, engage an alternative registered bank or licensed non-bank lender.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable on a statutory basis for offshore CAD/BIM drafting. If professional engineering advice is later provided in New Zealand, the Chartered Professional Engineers of New Zealand Act 2002 applies via the Registration Authority; the voluntary industry association is Engineering New Zealand (Ipōkere Aotearoa). Building-related output must comply with the New Zealand Building Code administered by MBIE.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None - no statutory operating licence or manufacturing permit is required for ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330 computer-aided design (CAD) and Building Information Modeling (BIM) services under New Zealand law; the company is expressly designated 'requires_statutory_license: false'.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) Te Mana Rauhī Taiao (nationally significant proposals); local territorial authority (for any resource consent under the Resource Management Act 1991)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 4 (No EIA). Pure digital services produce no physical discharge, and no EIA, resource consent, or discharge permit is triggered. If the company leases an office in New Zealand, landlord obligations under the Building Act 2004 and Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 apply, and the office tenancy must have a current building Warrant of Fitness.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the electronic CAD/BIM output. For auxiliary office operations: wastewater enters the municipal sewer under the Local Government Act 2002; electronic waste (e-waste) is managed under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; printing/plotting emissions (VOCs) remain below the permitted-activity limits of the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) 2004, requiring no resource consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ): evacuation scheme and fire safety certification for commercial premises under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 and the Fire Safety and Evacuation Procedures Regulations 2006, including an annual evacuation trial for premises with more than 100 occupants. Building control: a building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) and compliance schedule issued by the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004 for the leased office. Workplace safety: compliance with WorkSafe New Zealand requirements under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a general risk assessment, emergency planning, workstation ergonomics, and in-service electrical safety testing to AS/NZS 3760.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) — the national tax administration of New Zealand; official online portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz; complementary business registration portal: New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) at https://www.business.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident International Company (ELF_CUSTOM_CK_IC) conducting exclusively offshore BIM/CAD engineering services without a New Zealand fixed establishment, New Zealand-sourced income, or GST nexus in New Zealand is generally outside the New Zealand tax net and is not required to obtain an IRD number. If the entity establishes a New Zealand branch, derives New Zealand-source income, supplies goods or services in New Zealand, or employs personnel in New Zealand, it must apply for an IRD number via myIR using form IR742 (for companies) or IR596 (for non-resident companies). The application must be accompanied by: (1) certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents; (2) register of directors and ultimate shareholders; (3) registered office and principal place of business address; (4) a New Zealand address for service (which may be a registered tax agent's address); and (5) evidence of a NZBN or business registration. For GST purposes, the same IRD number is used as the GST registration number; a non-resident must register through myIR when taxable supplies in New Zealand exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period, including remote services supplied to New Zealand consumers. Voluntary GST registration is available to non-residents to claim input credits if the entity carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand. IRD typically processes registration within 5–10 business days; a New Zealand tax agent may file on the entity's behalf.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Tax Administration Act 1994. A non-resident International Company with no New Zealand fixed establishment and no New Zealand-source income is effectively tax-exempt in New Zealand: foreign-sourced offshore income is not taxed, and no GST registration is required absent a New Zealand taxable activity. Relevant statutory elections available include: (1) GST cash-basis accounting election for businesses with taxable turnover below NZD 2 million per annum; (2) GST election to zero-rate land supplies where the recipient is a GST-registered person; (3) hybrid mismatch elections under subpart FE of the Income Tax Act 2007 to address hybrid entity or hybrid instrument mismatches; (4) branch equivalent tax elections for controlled foreign company attributions; and (5) group loss transfer elections available only to qualifying New Zealand-resident group companies. No separate 'tax-exempt zone' election exists; the tax-exempt outcome flows from the entity's non-resident status and absence of New Zealand-source activity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a broad-based value-added tax administered by Inland Revenue under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (annual taxable supplies in New Zealand over any 12-month period); non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' (including digital and engineering services) to New Zealand consumers also cross the mandatory registration threshold at NZD 60,000; voluntary registration is available for non-residents with a New Zealand business presence or who intend to claim input tax credits
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based electronic stamping, or continuous transaction controls. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL network through the New Zealand e-Invoicing framework; Inland Revenue does not pre-clear or digitally stamp tax invoices. Tax invoices, credit notes, and export substantiation records must be retained for 7 years. Where PEPPOL-format e-invoices are used, they must conform to the New Zealand e-Invoicing specification, but no government fiscal stamp or electronic clearance obligation exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: GST zero-rating applies where goods are supplied for export and are physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply (or such longer period as approved by Inland Revenue), provided the supplier holds contemporaneous export evidence and the recipient is a non-resident or the goods are delivered to a place outside New Zealand. Services: zero-rating applies to services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, unless the services are directly connected with New Zealand land, performed personally by a natural person physically present in New Zealand, or supplied in connection with moveable personal property situated in New Zealand. For offshore BIM/CAD structural drafting services (ISIC 7110 / NAICS 541330) delivered to a non-resident overseas client with no New Zealand land nexus and no performance of work in New Zealand, zero-rating is available where the supplier maintains a written contract, a GST tax invoice, evidence of the recipient's non-resident status, and payment evidence from outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (eCSD filed via the New Zealand Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/foreign exchange receipt evidencing payment from the non-resident buyer
Commercial Invoice and GST tax invoice
Independent evidence of export completion (carrier certificate, port authority confirmation, or inspection certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue audits zero-rated export claims by cross-matching Customs export declarations against GST returns, bank receipts, and invoices. Where export documentation is deficient, goods are diverted back to New Zealand, or services do not meet the zero-rating tests, the zero-rating is reversed and GST at 15% is clawed back with use-of-money interest running from the original adjustment date. Fraudulent or deliberately false zero-rating claims attract shortfall penalties of 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, and up to 150% for an abusive tax position, plus criminal prosecution under sections 141 and 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994 with fines and imprisonment available for evasion. Export documentation must be retained for at least 7 years to support any GST zero-rating or refund claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua) is the central bank and the statutory authority for monetary policy, prudential regulation, and the oversight of registered banks. New Zealand has no designated foreign-exchange-control agency other than the Reserve Bank acting through licensed registered banks, and no approval or reporting is required for the majority of FX transactions beyond transaction-level balance-of-payments statistical reporting undertaken by the banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand is an IMF Article VIII member, meaning the NZD is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There is no exchange-control restriction on current-account payments for CAD/BIM services, no requirement for central-bank allocation of foreign currency, and no restriction on the repatriation of capital, dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees. Practical remittance hurdles are documentary and tax-driven, not FX-approval-driven: the remitting bank must obtain a correct purpose code, evidence of the underlying transaction, and proof of withholding tax compliance where applicable. Non-resident dividend remittances are subject to Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at the applicable treaty rate (commonly 15% under the double-tax agreement, 30% in the absence of treaty relief); interest remittances attract NRWT at up to 15% unless an IRD-approved treaty or approved issuer levy structure is used. Capital injections and full return of the same capital are free from tax and FX approval, provided the bank records the original source of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters of engineering or BIM services may receive and retain USD, EUR, GBP, CNY, or any freely convertible currency in onshore or offshore foreign-currency accounts indefinitely. The only obligations are bank-level Balance of Payments International Transactions Reporting (ITR) for individual transactions above NZD 10,000 and ordinary anti-money-laundering verification of the exporter's underlying service contract. There is no requirement to convert export proceeds to NZD nor to liquidate foreign-currency balances by any date.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account only with an established New Zealand nexus

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditionally feasible as a receivables and payables payment rail, but not as a substitute for a licensed New Zealand bank for capital escrow, trade-finance issuance, or same-day NZD clearing. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, and Currencycloud may be used for foreign-currency disbursement and collection, provided the EMI is registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and, where applicable, holds an Australian AFSL/EMI equivalent accepted by the receiving bank. Legal constraints are material: an unregistered offshore EMI cannot open a settlement account in New Zealand, cannot issue commercial letters of credit, cannot provide a New Zealand domestic bank-account suffix, and may be blocked by tier-1 banks as an unacceptable route for capital-escrow or high-value settlement. Feasibility rating: B- (Conditionally Feasible) for operational treasury flows; D (Not Feasible) for regulated escrow, debt, and documentary-credit functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand AML/CFT regulations do not categorically require physical attendance for company account opening; each registered bank may accept remote electronic identity verification for directors who are natural persons. However, for a non-resident-owned International Company with no domestic revenue, no local employees, and a tax-exempt offshore classification, most tier-1 banks will apply at least one enhanced due diligence measure, typically: (a) a video-conference interview with the founding director and the beneficial owner; (b) notarised or apostilled identification for each director; (c) evidence of the company's registered office in New Zealand; and (d) a visit or confirmation by the external lawyer/accountant acting as local agent. If the company cannot produce a New Zealand business address or a local director, a general manager, or a licensed designated agent, physical appearance of one director or the agent at an NZ bank branch should be expected. Remote-only opening is available from selected tier-1 banks if the company has an existing NZBN, a New Zealand residential/office address, and a full UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to offshore holding layers and nominee directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an organisational chart showing the full chain to natural persons; certified beneficial-ownership declaration signed by the UBO; certified trust deed and trustee board resolution where a trust is the UBO; Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATCA) and Common Reporting Standard (CRS) declarations in the bank's prescribed form.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company status flagged by the bank's tax operations team as possibly artificial
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the certificate of incorporation, current Companies Office extract with the exact company type, the IRD residency assessment or non-resident determination, the registered office agreement, board minutes explaining the substantive commercial purpose of the CAD/BIM outsourcing, and copies of active engineering or BIM service contracts with arms-length pricing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors with no verifiable local address or economic footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the statutory directors' register, a reliable overseas address evidentiary packet (utility bill, bank statement, government identity card) for each director, proof of the registered New Zealand office or local authorised agent, and confirmation that the directors have passed independent electronic KYC verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipts from foreign clients in jurisdictions perceived as high-risk or sanctioned
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the executed service master agreement with each counterparty, UBO and sanctions exposure statement of the client, an invoice and milestone acceptance certificate for each CAD/BIM engagement, audit trail of the outsourcing platform, and a legal memorandum or jurisdiction risk score where the counterparty is in a high-risk country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large unexplained wire volume or rapid inbound capital injection shortly after incorporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the fully executed shareholder loan agreement or equity subscription agreement, source-of-wealth statements for the investing entity, bank statements from the originating bank showing the previous existence of funds, the New Zealand foreign-investment classification or exemption letter, and a board resolution authorising the precise transaction and treasury purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant protocol for inbound capital injection is a SWIFT MT103 for the cash leg, or an MT202 for cover, to the New Zealand operating account clearly identified in the beneficiary field with the beneficiary bank's BIC. The remittance instruction must include a tailored purpose code aligned with the bank's New Zealand International Transactions Reporting (ITR) classification, typically 'Capital contribution' or 'Shareholder loan' for equity/debt injection and 'Professional consultancy services' for service prepayments. The narrative field (field 70) should state 'CAPITAL INJECTION - CK_IC - [Resolution Date]' or 'LOAN - CK_IC - [Facility Agreement Reference]'. The bank will verify the source of funds through the originator's bank and the corporate authority packet: board resolution, constitutional document, share register if equity, executed facility agreement if debt, UBO declaration, and source-of-wealth evidence for amounts above applicable due-diligence thresholds. For payments from a connected offshore entity, a transfer-pricing memorandum and an IRD withholding-tax position (for interest) must be annexed where the bank requires a filing-ready record. Escrowed capital should be held in a segregated Capital Escrow Account with contractual instruction that release occurs only against verified drawdown triggers approved by the board.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The principal clearing rails for trade disbursements are: (1) SWIFT MT103 payments for clean contract settlement to subcontractors, software vendors, or external consultants; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600 for high-value procurement, where the NZ bank issues a documentary credit to the seller's bank and makes payment against presented transport/acceptance documents; (3) Documentary collections (DP/DA) for supplier relationships requiring title documentation rather than an undertaking; (4) SWIFT gpi for end-to-end tracking of payments to high-risk corridors; (5) New Zealand's Electronic Settlement System (ESAS) for same-day NZD transfers to domestic beneficiaries; and (6) central bank real-time gross settlement rails where the counterparty bank is a direct Reserve Bank participant. For CAD/BIM outsourcing disbursements, an MT103 with purpose code 'Trade services' and the underlying subcontract number in field 70 is the preferred rail; commercial letters of credit are used only when the counterparty requires a formal payment undertaking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (USD/NZD, EUR/NZD, AUD/NZD, GBP/NZD, CNY/NZD) with a licensed New Zealand registered bank, with maturities of up to five years for construction or BIM delivery cycles.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies not freely deliverable in the onshore NZD market (e.g., certain emerging-market currencies), executed with an RBNZ-registered bank or an offshore bank with approved internal credit and collateralisation.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) where the New Zealand company receives or pays fixed/floating flows in different currencies to hedge long-term project financing or capitalised lease obligations.
European-style FX options (call or put on USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, CNY) for contingent cash flows such as procurement bids or option-based construction milestones.
FX vanilla swaps combining a spot exchange and a forward exchange to manage temporary liquidity needs when capital is injected in one currency and disbursed in another.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form 11) for the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (NZCO), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deliverable must be filed each year by the company's annual return date, which falls on the anniversary of the company's incorporation date or on the altered annual return date registered with NZCO. Filing opens earlier in the month before the annual return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a NZD 1.50 per day penalty for each day overdue after the annual return date (NZD 1.50/day). Companies that remain overdue for more than 90 days are subject to registration removal procedures by the Companies Office, leading to administrative strike-off and dissolution of the International Company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation statement for the International Company records (shareholding and director details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deliverable must be filed concurrently with the Annual Return; NZCO requires confirmation of the company's register details as at the annual return date each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to agree with the pre-populated company information shown on the annual return renders the filing invalid; outstanding confirmations can result in the annual return being treated as not filed, accruing late filing penalties and triggering administrative strike-off of the International Company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax declaration (previously deemed non-filing basis; for tax-exempt zone status, the international company is not required to file a separate annual income tax return unless a valid election for New Zealand tax treatment is made)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No statutory annual filing deadline applies where the International Company is treated as a foreign company with income exempt in New Zealand under the applicable tax-exempt zone rules; if a tax declaration is triggered, the annual Due Date for Income Tax (terminal tax) is the 7th day of the month following the provisional tax due date for the corresponding income year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Where a filing is nonetheless required, non-lodgment can lead to late filing penalties of NZD 100, interest assessments, and administrative non-compliance notices from IRD; persistent non-compliance can result in enforcement action against the International Company's New Zealand registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit applies to the International Company if it has consolidated total assets exceeding NZD 9 million at balance date, or total revenue exceeding NZD 15 million in each of the two immediately preceding accounting periods, or if the company is a company in respect of which an audit is required by the Companies Act 1993 or by its constitutive documents. For a wholly owned foreign-controlled International Company that is not required to file financial statements under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, audit exemption remains available provided the company is not otherwise an FMC reporting entity and shareholders unanimously consent to the audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalent to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) for Tier 1 and Tier 2 for-profit entities; New Zealand International Public Sector Accounting Standards (NZ IPSAS) if public sector; Small and Medium-Sized Entities elect to apply the New Zealand Equivalent to the IFRS for SMEs (NZ IFRS for SMEs), with FRS-42 adopted for Tier 2 not-for-profit entities. An International Company with exempt-company status is not required to file annual financial statements under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 unless it exceeds the large reporting entity thresholds or is a FMC reporting entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand law does not maintain a separate recurring UBO annual filing for an exempt International Company. However, the Companies Act 1993 (as amended by the Companies (Protection of Beneficial Ownership Information) Amendment Regulations 2022) requires the company to maintain adequate and current beneficial ownership information in its internal register of a natural person, and every company must keep an Oversight and Accountable Register. On every review and annual return, the company must record any transfer of shares, issue of shares, or change of ultimate beneficial owners in the regime to ensure practical transparency provisions are kept accurate. The Companies Office receives beneficial ownership information only upon request by enforcement agencies pursuant to the search powers; the annual return requires the International Company to confirm the accuracy of its registered shareholding and director records, effectively constituting the annual confirmation of UBO-derived registered data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including beneficial ownership information of ultimate natural persons where applicable)
Register of Directors (Register of Directors/Overseas Directors)
Minute Book (all shareholder and board resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 to USD 900 per annum for a licensed registered office and legal representation in New Zealand
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 to USD 18,000 per annum where a full independent audit is triggered; minimal non-assurance compilation between USD 1,500 and USD 3,500 if the company remains audit-exempt

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in New Zealand. Material preferences include the 15% refundable Research and Development Tax Incentive (RDTI) for eligible civil infrastructure and BIM software development; the absence of a general capital gains tax on most asset disposals; full imputation credits for resident shareholders (irrelevant to non-resident shareholders); and confinement of the New Zealand tax base for non-resident companies to New Zealand-source income only. No 'tax-exempt zone' regime exists for International Companies in New Zealand.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward with no statutory time cap; subject to shareholder continuity of at least 49% and, for listed companies, the same-business test

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or via approved tax agents
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual IR4 return; in-year provisional tax instalments and imputation credit returns (where applicable)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return is due on 30 September following the balance date. Terminal tax is due on 7 February of the following year. Registered tax agent extensions may adjust the terminal tax and filing dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, IRD number, registered office and financial statement balance date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the New Zealand registered office address and a New Zealand resident tax agent or authorised contact for service of notices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting industry classification code (ISIC/ANZSIC equivalent; use engineering and BIM/structural drafting classification under ISIC 7110)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the engineering design activity code. Do not classify the entity as a passive investment vehicle unless bona fide.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income derived in New Zealand
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only New Zealand-source income. Foreign-source CAD/BIM outsourcing fees are generally outside the New Zealand tax net for a non-resident company without a fixed New Zealand establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure, including direct drafting costs, software licences, subcontract labour and R&D expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenditures incurred in deriving New Zealand-source income. Related-party recharges must satisfy transfer pricing and thin capitalisation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss for the income year, including tax loss carry-forward claimed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may utilise carried-forward losses only if the 49% shareholder continuity test is maintained throughout the continuity period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder continuity declaration and ultimate shareholder details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify ultimate non-resident beneficial owners and attach ownership records to support the loss continuity test and NRWT compliance obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account balance and resident withholding tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot utilise New Zealand imputation credits. All dividends must be managed through the NRWT framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation: tax at 28% on net taxable income, reduced by RDTI credit, resident withholding tax and provisional tax paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle terminal tax on 7 February. The company must ensure provisional tax instalments have been paid to avoid UOMI and late payment penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 per month for each month or part-month the IR4 remains overdue, capped at NZ$1,000 per return. Late payment penalties accrue in staged 1% increments up to a maximum of 4% of the unpaid tax. Use-of-money interest (UOMI) applies from the statutory payment date. Shortfall penalties apply separately for inaccurate returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) of 30% on non-imputed dividends; 15% on fully imputed dividends. Most DTA protocols reduce the portfolio rate to 15% and the direct-investment rate to 5% for a corporate shareholder holding 10% or more of the voting power.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home revenue authority and deliver it to the New Zealand withholding agent before payment, together with the Inland Revenue declaration (IR902 or online equivalent) confirming treaty residence. The withholding agent retains the TRC for audit. Where the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test applies, Inland Revenue may require evidence of genuine economic substance before honouring treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT rate 15%, generally reduced to 10% under DPAs, with the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% available as an alternative for qualifying arm's length loans to unrelated non-resident lenders. Royalties: statutory NRWT rate 15%, with treaty rates typically 5% or 10% depending on the counterparty jurisdiction and IP character.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory NZD filing threshold for mandatory Local File or Master File exists in New Zealand. Inland Revenue applies the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines through subpart FG and expects contemporaneous arm's length documentation for all material cross-border related-party transactions. In practice, IRD audit attention is typically triggered where related-party sales or service fees exceed NZ$10 million in aggregate, but documentation must be able to support pricing at any level of materiality.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations of the Caribbean/UAE statutory form. Economic substance is enforced indirectly through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section BG 1), thin capitalisation rules, transfer pricing provisions, the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test, and the requirement that a company claiming New Zealand tax residence maintain its centre of effective management and real operational substance in New Zealand. A purported 'tax-exempt International Company' engaged in BIM and structural drafting without office premises, employees, or board control in New Zealand faces treaty denial, GAAR recharacterisation, and penalty exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating New Zealand-source income, falsifying CAD/BIM service invoices, suppressing cash or wire receipts, or claiming fictitious deductible expenses in the IR4 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax under the Tax Administration Act 1994; criminal prosecution with fines up to NZ$250,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years; seizure of company assets and management intervention by Inland Revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in evasion face personal criminal conviction, restitution orders for the unpaid tax, Departure Prohibition Orders preventing travel from New Zealand, and civil liability for reckless trading under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an International Company with no office, no employees, no director meetings, and no economic substance while shifting profits from a substantive BIM engineering business into the purported 'tax-exempt zone' structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the structure under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section BG 1); recomputation of taxable income on an arm's length basis; shortfall penalties of 40%–100% for abusive tax positions; potential strike-off of the company register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for debts arising from reckless trading, ordered to restore company funds, subjected to travel bans, and disqualified from managing companies in New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting related-party fees for civil infrastructure drafting, BIM modelling, or software services at a non-arm's length rate without a documented comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustment by the Commissioner plus use-of-money interest; shortfall penalties ranging from 20% for an unacceptable tax position to 40% for gross carelessness; disallowance of non-compliant intercompany deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing declarations or knowingly approve fraudulent intercompany pricing may be pursued personally for civil restitution of the tax shortfall and face criminal fraud charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repatriating profits via Wire Transfer or Wise payment rails to non-resident shareholders without deducting NRWT; failing to perform customer due diligence or file suspicious-transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer becomes personally liable for the un-withheld NRWT, plus shortfall penalties of up to 150%; AML/CFT Act offences attract fines up to NZ$2,000,000 per offence for entities and imprisonment for up to 7 years for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for AML failures committed with their authority, consent, or connivance; statutory director penalties apply for unpaid NRWT under the Tax Administration Act; Departure Prohibition Orders may be issued against them.
